clue.text: Pip was entitled to great ones

definitions.text: Pip was entitled to great ones

parts.words: Pip was entitled to great ones
parts.note: Pip is the hero of the Dickens novel whose title begins with 'Great', so 'entitled' puns on the book's name rather than on his rights

explanation.surface: A young man named Pip had a right to some impressive inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' looks like 'having a right to', but it means 'given a title': Dickens's Pip appears in a book called Great ___.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dickens novel about Pip is titled after his hopes of fortune, his anticipations of wealth.

clue.text: Approve the Cockney's mount at the finish

parts.note: the finish is the end

indicators.note: the Cockney's says the word is spoken the London way, dropping its initial H

parts.note: a horse is a mount

explanation.surface: A Londoner's horse gets the nod at the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their Hs, so 'the Cockney's' takes the H off HORSE to give ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to give official backing, a synonym for sanction.

clue.text: Civil Service prose is terrible, of course

indicators.note: is terrible says the letters are in a terrible state, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Civil servants write dreadful prose, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is terrible' rearranges CS and PROSE together. 'Of course' looks like 'naturally', but 'course' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a course of action or series of steps.

clue.text: Trick angles for swimmers

parts.note: cod as a verb means to hoax or trick
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A sneaky fishing technique for catching swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: COD as a verb (to fool) is British slang; 'angles' looks like corners but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod are fish, creatures that swim.

clue.text: Motorists crowding round can upset a girl

indicators.note: crowding round says the motoring letters surround what follows

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Drivers gather round and knock over a girl's can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where the can is turned upside down; 'crowding round' has the motoring organisation surround it. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita is a female first name.

clue.text: One river animal found in the country

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope by a river is spotted somewhere in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation of the British Isles, so a country.

clue.text: Revere's exploit reported in the compound

indicators.note: reported says the word is what you hear spoken

parts.note: Paul Revere's famous exploit was his midnight ride in 1775, a night ride

explanation.surface: An account of Paul Revere's famous feat appears in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode at night in 1775 to warn of British troops. 'Compound' looks like an enclosure but means a chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitride is a chemical combination of nitrogen with another element.

clue.text: It's. a boon, perhaps, to protect men of letters from blacking out

indicators.note: to protect says the rearranged letters wrap around and shield what follows
perhaps says the letters of boon may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: the literati are learned people, men of letters

explanation.surface: A gift might shield scholars from losing consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging 'boon', whose letters then split around the scholars as 'to protect' says. 'Blacking out' looks like fainting but here means erasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliteration is the wiping out or covering over of something, as in blacking out text.

clue.text: "A tinker out of _____, a vagrant oft in quod" (Kipling)

definitions.text: "A tinker out of _____, a vagrant oft in quod" (Kipling)

parts.words: "A tinker out of _____, a vagrant oft in quod" (Kipling)
parts.note: a Kipling line describing John Bunyan, the tinker preacher jailed (in quod, slang for prison) in his home county town; the blank is that town

explanation.surface: A line of Kipling's verse about a wandering tinker often in prison, with one place name left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Holy War' calls John Bunyan a tinker from his home town, where he was jailed and wrote The Pilgrim's Progress. 'Quod' is old British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan came from and was imprisoned in this English county town, which fills the gap in Kipling's line.

clue.text: Thought one old fashioned about English

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the inserted letter

parts.note: old-fashioned means dated

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a person was rather out of date regarding English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside DATED, giving DEATED, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ideated is to have formed an idea, so it is a past-tense synonym of having conceived mentally.

clue.text: Carpeting of fertiliser on the hill

parts.note: a dressing is manure or fertiliser spread on land
a down is a rolling chalk hill, as in the South Downs

explanation.surface: Spreading manure on the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' in British English is a telling-off ('to be carpeted'), not floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding, being hauled in for a reprimand, is a carpeting.

clue.text: Sabra, for example, is artist, as well as priest

definitions.note: a sabra is one person, a native-born citizen, matching the noun sense of the answer

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A sabra is described as both a painter and a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: A sabra is a Jew born in the land of Israel; the word looks like a name but is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabra is a native-born citizen of the Jewish state, so is one instance of its nationals.

clue.text: Girl takes cereal out of greed

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A girl grabs some breakfast cereal purely out of greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is a link meaning 'comes from', not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is a synonym for greed, an excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Girl the Poles are after makes uniform

indicators.note: are after says the letters for the poles come after the girl's name

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
N and S stand for the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A girl's Polish pursuers make her conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Poles' looks like people from Poland, but means the magnetic north and south poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something is to level it or make it smooth and consistent throughout.

clue.text: Man with' the skill to make a bowler perhaps

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
address can mean skill or dexterity, as in handling things with address

explanation.surface: A skilled craftsman who can make a bowler hat.
explanation.walkthrough: ADDRESS in the old sense of adroitness or skill is the less familiar meaning; a bowler is a British hard felt hat, not the cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a type of hat, an example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: Go with' Bill and his guests

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
your guests are your company

explanation.surface: Join Bill and his visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany is to escort or travel alongside.

clue.text: Since gala is ruined, this will ease the discomfort

indicators.note: is ruined says the letters of the two words before it are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Since the gala was a disaster, here is something to soothe the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ruined' rearranges SINCE GALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a drug that relieves pain, which is what this describes.

clue.text: Offensive from a carrier leading to one victory in Europe

parts.note: a bus carries passengers
Roman I is one

explanation.surface: An attack launched from an aircraft carrier brings a victory in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' suggests a military push, as does 'carrier' (warship), but it is the adjective meaning insulting.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means insulting or rude, so hurtful in speech.

clue.text: Sesame producing drink? Grand! The Italian one

parts.note: gin is a drink
G stands for grand, a thousand
il is Italian for the
Roman I is one

explanation.surface: Someone offered a sesame drink exclaims that it is grand, the Italian one.
explanation.walkthrough: Gingili is the Indian name for sesame and its oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingili is another name for the sesame plant, whose seeds give oil.

clue.text: Tree played a part in "Diana's Penance"

indicators.note: played a part in says the answer is a run of letters forming part of the title that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tree took a role in a play called Diana's Penance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Tree played' as the definition, but 'played' adds nothing to 'Tree' and belongs with 'a part in', the signal that the answer sits inside 'Diana's Penance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a kind of poplar, a tree with trembling leaves.

clue.text: Country taking an apprentice from another

indicators.note: taking says letters are taken away from the second country

parts.note: another country here is a different nation, the one down under
an gives A
L is a learner, an apprentice

explanation.surface: One nation recruits an apprentice from a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' removes A and L (a learner, as on British L-plates) from AUSTRALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A central European nation, so a country.

clue.text: Ill state of the grasslands

explanation.surface: A sick state of affairs out on the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' is not sick but the abbreviation for Illinois, nicknamed the Prairie State; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is known as the state of grassland plains, and the wide treeless grassland of North America is called that too.

clue.text: Soldier returns to sauna, excited by such creatures

indicators.note: returns says the soldier's letters come back the other way

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: excited says the letters of sauna are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier goes back to the sauna, roused by some reptiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GI into IG, and 'excited' rearranges SAUNA into UANAS; the whole clue reads as a description of the lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large tropical lizards, the reptiles the clue's picture gestures towards.

clue.text: Way to drink and make music

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A way to have a drink and make music.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings, so to play an instrument.

clue.text: Leading player in disgrace is hot stuff

indicators.note: in says the star goes inside the disgrace word

parts.note: your name is mud when you are in disgrace
the star is the leading player in a show

explanation.surface: A star player has fallen into disgrace, yet is still in demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the leading player inside the disgrace word, from 'your name is mud'. 'Hot stuff' looks like praise for the player but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard is a pungent condiment, a spicy, fiery thing.

clue.text: More clamorous than the first and second? That's right

parts.note: the first is number one, written No. I
ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether one thing is louder than the first and second, then agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: NO I is 'No. 1' with the numeral as I; 'That's' expands to 'that is', abbreviated IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of loud, describing something that makes more din.

clue.text: First class side boasted of being fliers

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 written as I
R for right, one side
crew is an old past tense of crow, meaning boasted

explanation.surface: A top-class team bragged about being pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW as the past tense of 'crow' (to brag) is the old form; A1 becomes AI with the numeral read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the team that flies a plane, so its members are airmen.

clue.text: Junior barrister perhaps wishes to appear happy-go-lucky

parts.note: in English law a devil is a junior barrister doing work for a senior
may means perhaps, as in it may rain
to care to do something is to wish to do it

explanation.surface: A trainee lawyer apparently wants to look carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: A DEVIL is a British legal term for a junior barrister who takes on a senior's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care describes a reckless, carefree attitude, the same as a cheerfully casual one.
